description:
DECISION GATE. No other core-exec-* item may start until this ADR is accepted by the user.

Problem: PR #2781 added a Polars-only platform option named `engine`. A generic word now means one thing on one platform while the same word means other things elsewhere: Firebolt `engine_name`/`engine_type`/`engine_size` is a compute resource (recorded as platform_compute.engine), Athena records the literal product name as platform_compute.engine="athena", and the anonymizer hashes every key named `engine` (anonymization_specs.yaml:79) with a Polars-only exemption (:142-152). Research across all 52 manifest platforms, planned platforms and the gateway plan found ~12 names for a compute resource (warehouse, engine_name, workgroup, cluster_id, http_path, spark_pool_name, service_id, application_id, cluster_identifier, cluster_name, resource_class...), four Polars streaming controls (option `streaming`, option `engine`, tuning execution.streaming_mode and execution.engine_affinity, where engine_affinity="in-memory" is silently ignored), `execution_mode` meaning both sql/dataframe and lazy/eager, and result identity that cannot tell engine variants apart.

Write docs/development/adr/adr-core-execution-variants.md (follow the existing ADR format in docs/development/adr/) and get it accepted. The ADR must decide, each with the chosen option and the rejected alternatives:
D1 Taxonomy and the separation test: deployment (where it runs / who operates it), compute resource and size (named billable vendor object), execution engine (which execution machinery runs the query with deployment, compute and endpoint held fixed), gateway (intermediary that may reroute/rewrite), observed engine (the observed leg of execution engine, not a separate setting). State what is NOT core: runtime version (record only), storage/table format, optimizer flags such as Spark AQE (tuning; see spark-session-config-model), dtype backend.
D2 Canonical names: execution_engine; compute_resource and compute_size; gateway (+ connection options gateway_host/port/protocol/ca_bundle); deployment keeps the platform:deployment selector. Result field names: config.execution_engine, platform.execution_engine{requested, applied, applied_class, applied_native, resolution, observed, observed_source}, queries[].execution_engine, platform.compute{resource, resource_kind, size}, platform.gateway{name, routed}, platform.deployment{selected, selected_class}, platform.variant holding the variant_id string.
D3 Execution-engine values: closed core class list (adaptive, in-memory, streaming, gpu, native-vectorized, standard, distributed, jit, delegated); reserved sentinel `default` (pass nothing; platforms cannot declare it); platforms declare named values in the manifest capability execution_engines {name: {class, display_name, description, dependencies, selectable}}; `selectable: false` for observed-only engines (e.g. Databricks Photon, Velox); same value name maps to the same class on every platform; value names equal the class name unless the variant is a vendor brand; name any other exception explicitly (e.g. Dask `threads`). Adapters implement one hook, resolve_execution_engine(requested) -> ExecutionEngineReceipt, with a base default that accepts only `default`.
D4 Requested/applied/observed: how `default` is resolved by introspection (never by version string), the resolution enum (explicit | tuning_profile | legacy_option | version_default | platform_default), observed values at run level (declared name | mixed | not_captured) and at query level (declared name | unknown), and why the two differ; observed_source (explain | vendor_log | session_var | none).
D5 Precedence and conflicts: explicit CLI/MCP/config > tuning profile > legacy option > default. Decide exactly what happens when a legacy option (e.g. Polars streaming=true) is given together with an explicit execution_engine that disagrees: the explicit value wins with a warning, or the run fails. Fate of the Polars `streaming` option and --polars-streaming (deprecated alias) and the Polars `engine` option (removed without alias only if unreleased; see gate G2). Tuning execution.engine_affinity/streaming_mode become the tuning-file spelling of the requested engine; decide whether smart defaults (core/dataframe/tuning/defaults.py ~L176-182, which choose an engine by scale) keep choosing an engine once the value is honored.
D6 Result schema 2.3 field shapes, reader behavior for 2.2 bundles, and the legacy mapping (platform_options.streaming=true; platform.config.engine_requested in the 120 Polars matrix bundles, where `default` maps to resolution=version_default; Athena's old platform_compute.engine field).
D7 Anonymization, consistent with docs/development/adr/adr-published-identifier-field-set.md: whether compute_resource is dropped at publication (no consumer) or kept hashed (named consumer), resource_kind/size readable, core vocabulary keys readable, Athena's literal engine field renamed (e.g. product), Polars exemption removed.
D8 Identity: variant_id = platform_id [~deployment if not the manifest default] [+requested engine if not default] [@gateway]; requested (not applied) defines identity; display labels are derived separately; where variant_id is used (Explorer read model, corpus identity, labels, ranking exclusion for gateway runs).
D9 Gateway as a core manifest capability gateways {name: {routes_to: {engine: {class}}, requires_host}}, reconciled with the locked decisions in the gateway plan (/Users/joe/.jcode/scratch/espresso-greybeam-plan-v2.md: values native/espresso/greybeam/custom, tpc_compliant false, baseline guard, cost suppression, no proxy_* names, connection options never via MCP). The core owns the comparability guard (variants_comparable) and its wiring into compare, regression and analytics.
D10 Surface per adr-one-engine-scoped-surfaces.md: one core validator used by both CLI and MCP; CLI --execution-engine (and later --gateway); MCP run_benchmark/start_benchmark execution_engine parameter with one core contract entry; compute_resource and gateway connection options are not MCP parameters; deprecated MCP keys (Polars streaming, clickhouse deployment_mode) keep resolving through the core during the deprecation window.
D11 Reserved bare words: no newly registered canonical option key may be engine, mode, backend, runtime, executor or warehouse; enumerate today's grandfathered keys from the live registry (PlatformHookRegistry specs, cli/platform_defaults.py, MCP allowlist) and assign each to the change that removes it (deployment or compute unification). Decide Fabric DW `warehouse` (a database there, not compute).
D12 Alias rule: whether deprecated aliases (mode, warehouse, deployment, force_execution, use_distributed, streaming) count as registered keys for D11 and the parity test while their deprecation window runs, and how the parity test distinguishes canonical keys from aliases.
D13 Deprecation and migration: the length of the deprecation window (e.g. one minor release), how aliases are removed afterwards, release-note requirements (CHANGELOG [Unreleased] and the upgrade notes) for every public CLI, MCP and schema change, and how existing saved YAML configs and credential profiles holding native keys (warehouse, deployment_mode, streaming, engine_name, workgroup) keep working or are migrated.
